writeup: TIC 367193047 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 2.191730 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The primary eclipse produces a 4.55% dimming, while no secondary eclipse was detected. The brightness dip shows a high detection significance with a BLS signal-to-noise ratio of 455.4, and pixel-level image analysis confirms the signal at a peak signal-to-noise of 36.2, though the centroid offset of 3.5 arcsec from the target warrants note. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs. However, the alternating eclipse depths show a significant odd/even z-score of 5.79, indicating the true orbital period is double the initial automated estimate. While pixel-level confirmation and eclipse timing remain unaffected by this data-quality flag, the period ambiguity represents an open question about this candidate system.
